newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Inex and Mercedes set up Yugo joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Inex and Mercedes set up Yugo joint venture.

text.p: Inex Intereksport of Belgrade and Stuttgart's Daimler-Benz AG have set up a joint venture company to market Mercedes-Benz vehicles in Yugoslavia, Mercedes-Benz country director Diether Mudrak said on Tuesday.

"The Mercedes-Benz Yugoslavia joint venture is the first such shareholding company founded in the country since new laws on enterprises and foreign investments were passed," Mudrak told a news conference.
Mercedes-Benz AG will own 51 percent and Inex 49 percent of the capital, Mudrak said and announced a 10 million German mark investment over the next few months.
Part of the initial capital of 9-10 million marks will be real estate and other property invested by Inex.
Mercedes will provide the balance in the form of funds and equipment to refurbish premises for its Yugoslav sales and service branch Autokuca Inex.
"Mercedes-Benz initially plans to open another 10 to 20 service and sales points, but this will depend on market growth," Mudrak said.
The company also plans cooperation with local bus and truck makers Neobus, Ikarbus and FAP.
Mudrak expected sales to meet import quotas set by the government to protect the local vehicle manufacturing industry.
"These change every year and we hope to get bigger quotas in the future," he told Reuters.
"We hope to sell 600 cars in 1997, as well as a certain number of commercial vehicles," Mudrak said without specifying.
The basic price for models offered ranged from 38,800 marks for the C-180 to 196,900 marks for the CL-600 Coupe, excluding costs of transport, customs duties and taxes.
Customs duties and taxes push prices of imported vehicles up by as much as 60 percent on the Yugoslav market.
Mercedes-Benz will hold an official exhibition in Belgrade on Wednesday -- the first in Yugoslavia since the break up of the former federation in 1991.
